 SPOKANE, Wash. — The No. 22 Gonzaga Bulldogs (2-1) return to McCarthey Athletic Center as they host the Montana State Bobcats (2-2) on Tuesday.
 Tipoff is set for 8 p.m. from The Kennel, with the game airing on CBS Sports Network.
 This will be the 72nd all-time meeting between the two programs, although they have not faced one another since 1996, when the Zags won 91-76. The very first matchup took place in 1914, with the Bobcats taking a 29-16 win in Bozeman. Gonzaga leads the all-time series 36-35, and head coach Mark Few has a 46-1 all-time record against Big Sky Conference opponents.
 ABOUT NO. 22 GONZAGA 
 Gonzaga enters the matchup with Montana State after dropping eight spots in the AP Top 25 poll following an 81-80 loss to LSU at the Spokane Arena on Saturday.
 Through three games this season, Gonzaga is averaging 89.0 points, 35.3 rebounds, 17.3 assists, 7.3 steals and 7.7 turnovers per game while shooting 49% from the field, 42.1% from 3-point range and 71.4% from the free throw line.
 The Zags saw those numbers dip across the board in their matchup with LSU, scoring 80 points on 44.6% shooting from the field, 29.4% from 3-point range and 64.3% from the free throw line against the Tigers.
 Sophomore guard Davis Fogle leads the Bulldogs in scoring, averaging 19.7 points per game on 43.2% shooting and 31.3% from 3-point range, while also giving the Zags 5.7 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 2.0 steals per game.
 Fifth-year forward Braden Huff is leading the team in rebounding with 6.7 per game, while also scoring 16.0 points per game on 52.5% shooting. Huff has also provided three steals and two blocks in three games of action.
 Two other Zags are averaging double-figure scoring numbers, with sophomore guard Isiah Harwell scoring 12.7 points per game on 55.6% shooting from the floor and 50% from the 3-point line. Fifth-year guard Xavian Lee is providing 11.0 points and a team-high 5.0 assists per game on 47.4% shooting and 50% from 3-point territory.
 Junior forward Izan Almansa did not play in Gonzaga's game against New Mexico State, but is averaging 9.5 points per game and gave the Zags a big boost against LSU, going for eight points and hauling in seven rebounds against the Tigers.
 In the latest KenPom rankings, the Bulldogs sit at No. 13 overall, with the fifth-best offensive rating and the 34th-best defensive rating.
 ABOUT MONTANA STATE 
 Montana State enters this matchup at 2-2, with wins over Long Beach State and Cal Poly and losses to Colorado State and BYU. In the Bobcats' most recent game, they took down Cal Poly 77-52 in Bozeman.
 Christian King and Jeremiah Davis lead the team in scoring, both averaging 13.8 points to go along with 4.5 rebounds per game. The 6-foot-4 Davis has also racked up seven steals on the season while shooting 61.3% from the floor and 46.7% from 3-point range. The 6-foot-8 King is shooting 46.7% from the field and 38.5% from beyond the arc.
 The Bobcats returned three All-Big Sky honorees from a season ago in Davis (All-Defensive Team), King (Honorable Mention) and fifth-year guard Jed Miller (First Team). Miller did not play against Colorado State, but in three games of action is averaging 9.3 points, 3.0 assists and 2.7 rebounds per game on 40.9% shooting.
 Montana State was picked as the preseason favorite in the Big Sky in both the preseason coaches and media polls.
 GONZAGA VS. MONTANA STATE BETTING ODDS, PREVIEW, PREDICTION 
 Spread: Gonzaga -24.5
 Total: Over/under 153.5
 Gonzaga has dominated Big Sky Conference opponents under head coach Mark Few, holding a 46-1 all-time record against the conference throughout the Few era. Despite the robust record, Montana State is a team that will provide a challenge even for top-tier teams like Gonzaga. Against BYU, a team that has an offensive ranking one spot higher than the Zags according to KenPom, Montana State lost by just 15 points, covering the 21.5-point spread.
 However, BYU has the 81st-ranked defense compared to Gonzaga with the 34th-ranked defense. Factoring that into the equation, and given the need for a bounce-back game after the loss to LSU, the Zags may make life far more difficult for Montana State.
 Give me the Zags -24.5, and I like over 153.5, too.
